title: The assistant that read a private repo
blurb: The draft keyed context by path without checking repository access.
prompt: An external audit found completions that quoted code from a repository the requesting user could not read, because the draft trusted file paths in the request. The same cache served a force-pushed repo's dead symbols. Review it, fix it, and prove repository access and index freshness are enforced.
aiNote: The draft treats a caller-supplied file path as sufficient authority to read repository content, so context from any repo can be completed on, and it caches the index by repo name alone, so a force-push keeps serving deleted symbols.
testIdea: Request a completion whose path points into a repo the caller cannot read and assert 403; push a new commit and assert the next completion is a cache miss and the status reports the new sha; assert a completion on a repo more than ten commits behind is refused.
followUps: Should rejected completions be training signal, and with what privacy boundary?
How would you budget context when a file is larger than the token cap?
What makes a symbol index trustworthy after a rebase?
